Phase 4 Docker integration discovers and executes the workspace phase-four-checker Agent definition.

Phase 6 Docker integration loads the compacted vendor transcript after stopping its isolated Agent process and preserves the Agent session identity.
Phase 6 Docker integration resumes a compacted transcript after simulating a prior vendor commit and records a successful cross-version compatibility result.

capabilities.known_gap: Lodestone is compiled into the kernel but its anchor lifecycle is not observable through ACP.

capabilities.evidence: Phase 6 Context projection preserves cache usage fields when the prompt response supplies them and otherwise displays them as unavailable; the internal cache-break state has no ACP event.
capabilities.known_gap: ACP prompt usage may expose cache token counts, but prompt cache break detection state is not separately observable.

capabilities.evidence: Phase 6 consumes ACP usage_update used/size values, persists the context-window projection, and renders exact unavailable states for budget fields ACP omits.
capabilities.known_gap: ACP exposes context utilization but no dedicated token-budget configuration or remaining-budget event.

capabilities.evidence: Phase 7 persists Goal status, continuation count, token budget, completion evidence, blocked audit, and idempotent background intent records.
Goal completion and blocked transitions are exposed through the durable Harness API; missing completion evidence is rejected and continuation limits produce a blocked audit.
capabilities.known_gap: ACP GoalTool lifecycle is not a durable service boundary; Harness state is authoritative for continuation and audit semantics.

capabilities.evidence: The terminal Goal command is catalogued as blocked because ACP available_commands_update does not advertise local-jsx commands.
capabilities.known_gap: Goal command UI depends on the vendor terminal lifecycle; the Harness Goal API is a durable adapter, not a claim of ACP command parity.

capabilities.evidence: Worker discovers .claude/workflows files inside the mounted workspace, hashes source content, and emits definitions through the existing ACP-bound Worker channel.
Workflow runs persist definitions, ordered steps, attempts, retry state, output, cancellation, and terminal audit state.
capabilities.known_gap: Workflow execution is represented by Harness-managed ACP prompts; vendor local command UI remains outside ACP.

capabilities.evidence: The terminal Workflow browser is not advertised through ACP; Worker-side workspace discovery and the Harness run API preserve the executable definition boundary.
capabilities.known_gap: ACP cannot invoke the vendor local-jsx Workflow browser.

capabilities.evidence: Cron schedules persist explicit IANA timezone, misfire policy, catch-up bound, next run, and lifecycle timestamps.
Cancelling a Cron schedule atomically cancels its background job and records a cron.cancelled audit event.
Cron list state is read from PostgreSQL and remains available independently of browser/SSE connections.
The scheduler computes fixed interval and five-field occurrences with explicit timezone and deterministic misfire semantics.
capabilities.known_gap: Vendor Kairos daemon and local trigger command are not relied on by the ACP Web session.

capabilities.evidence: Harness scheduler owns durable clock, timezone, missed-run, and restart recovery behavior; vendor daemon is not double-managed.
capabilities.known_gap: The vendor Kairos daemon lifecycle is platform-bound and is represented by the Harness scheduler rather than claimed as ACP-native.

capabilities.evidence: Brief work can be submitted as a one-shot durable background job with owner, token budget, output cursor, attach, and stop state.
capabilities.known_gap: The vendor Brief-only terminal presentation and daemon lifecycle are not exposed by ACP.

capabilities.evidence: Away-summary work uses the same persisted one-shot background boundary and remains independent of browser connectivity.
capabilities.known_gap: The vendor useAwaySummary hook is mounted by the REPL UI and has no ACP lifecycle event.

capabilities.known_gap: BriefTool availability depends on terminal bootstrap state and is not directly advertised or invoked through ACP.

capabilities.known_gap: ACP available_commands_update does not expose local-jsx commands.

Sleeping background jobs use next_run_at and resume through the durable scheduler after a process or Gateway restart.
Background job logs are cursor-addressable and can be re-attached without depending on an active SSE subscriber.
The Web Automation panel exposes durable background status, log cursor, attach, and stop controls.
The vendor Monitor shortcut remains catalogued but blocked; Harness monitor jobs use the durable background API.
capabilities.known_gap: The terminal Monitor command is local-jsx and cannot be invoked through ACP available commands.

capabilities.known_gap: RemoteTrigger requires an external authenticated callback, provider credentials, and an ACP-visible registration lifecycle.

capabilities.known_gap: ACP available_commands_update does not expose the local-jsx trigger registry command.

capabilities.known_gap: TTY panel capture is outside the standard ACP Web session boundary.

capabilities.known_gap: Terminal panel support requires a separate terminal-capable ACP profile.

capabilities.known_gap: Rebuilding the vendor with WEB_BROWSER_TOOL is outside the locked-vendor Harness scope.

capabilities.evidence: HISTORY_SNIP is compiled=false; Snip is not treated as an Artifact.
capabilities.known_gap: Vendor feature must be compiled and exposed through ACP before enabling.

capabilities.evidence: REVIEW_ARTIFACT is compiled=false in the locked build and review semantics are not part of the registry contract.
capabilities.known_gap: Requires a vendor feature-enabled ACP review contract.

capabilities.known_gap: Real outbound fetch requires an enabled network policy and provider credentials.

capabilities.known_gap: Requires an authenticated, isolated remote profile.

capabilities.known_gap: Requires a separately authenticated remote control profile.

known_gaps.summary: The locked ACP fast path neither parses inline plugin directories nor initializes the LSP manager, so an installed language server cannot make LSPTool invocable.

evidence.detail: ACP mode is selected only when process.argv[2] is exactly --acp and immediately calls runAcpAgent.
runAcpAgent does not parse --plugin-dir or invoke initializeLspServerManager.
The optional image contains the binary and plugin but reports blocked and preserves a failed real ACP definition attempt.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add an upstream ACP bootstrap API for inline plugins and the LSP manager, then change the profile expected-failure test into a location-producing E2E.

known_gaps.summary: ACP prompt conversion does not deliver image content blocks to the model even though image output blocks are supported.

evidence.detail: The locked vendor explicitly disables promptCapabilities.image until multimodal input is wired.
Harness input controls remain disabled and preserve the expected failure.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Enable the input control only after ACP passes a real image block through prompt conversion and a model contract test.

known_gaps.summary: SSH remote execution requires host credentials and transport outside the standard ACP Web session.

evidence.detail: Only isolated LSP and Chromium profiles are provided; SSH is not mounted.
SSH is explicitly represented as blocked.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add an authenticated remote profile with a scoped workspace and ACP-visible lifecycle before enabling.

known_gaps.summary: Bridge and Direct Connect are TTY/remote-control integrations rather than standard ACP session operations.

evidence.detail: No bridge transport is exposed by the base stack.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Keep the capability blocked until a separately authenticated Web transport and audit contract exists.

known_gaps.summary: Voice mode requires a browser/media adapter and is not available through ACP stdio.

evidence.detail: Voice is retained as an explicit platform gap.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Implement a browser voice adapter with explicit permission and retention controls.

known_gaps.summary: Notifications and SCM/PR callbacks require external credentials and opt-in integration profiles.

evidence.detail: Platform status reports these integrations as not_tested without credentials.
Base Docker does not accept external callback credentials.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add provider-specific opt-in profiles with callback authentication and end-to-end audit tests.

known_gaps.summary: The vendor ACP notification converter supports terminal tool results, but the forwarding loop skips the user SDK message that carries tool_result; DeepHarness recovery is post-persistence rather than ACP-native or live.

evidence.detail: The ACP forwarding switch skips SDK user messages instead of passing tool_result blocks to toAcpNotifications.
Real ACP tool execution reaches in_progress and the model receives the result, but no native terminal tool_call_update is observed before prompt completion.
The Harness uses a read-only, bounded transcript reconciliation adapter to recover persisted terminal output after ACP prompt completion.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Track an upstream ACP fix that forwards user tool_result blocks as terminal tool_call_update notifications, then remove the post-persistence adapter and assert native live output.

known_gaps.summary: ACP session/request_permission returns only a selected option ID and cannot carry AskUserQuestion updatedInput.answers.

evidence.detail: Harness records answers and uses a same-turn follow-up prompt because the ACP outcome schema has no updated input field.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Track an upstream ACP fix that permits a permission response to return updated tool input, then replace the compatibility follow-up with native answers.

known_gaps.summary: Agent workers assemble an independent tool pool and custom Agent definitions can override restrictive parent permission modes before ACP exposes a Harness-acknowledged prelaunch policy point; post-observation cancellation cannot provide an atomic no-expansion guarantee.

evidence.detail: The vendor builds the child worker tool pool independently with the Agent definition permission mode or acceptEdits.
A custom Agent definition can override the parent permission mode for the spawned query.
Harness detects late Agent input permission expansion and cancels the outer ACP prompt, which is conservative but post-observation.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add an ACP pre-tool authorization request or session policy contract that can reject Agent launch and constrain child mode/tools before vendor execution begins.

known_gaps.summary: The locked vendor compiles coordinator mode, but activation is a local-jsx command and ACP only publishes prompt commands, so Web sessions cannot enter the native coordinator mode.

evidence.detail: Coordinator activation is implemented as a local-jsx command.
The current ACP surface has no coordinator mode configuration operation.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Expose coordinator activation and status as an ACP session configuration capability with explicit tool and quota semantics.

known_gaps.summary: ListPeers is guarded by the optional UDS_INBOX build feature, which is not compiled into the locked default vendor build and therefore cannot be discovered or invoked through ACP.

evidence.detail: ListPeers is conditionally imported only when feature('UDS_INBOX') is compiled.
The real ACP test asserts SearchExtraTools/ExecuteExtraTool returns a not-found failure without creating a false peer projection.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Provide a separately reviewed vendor build profile with UDS_INBOX or an ACP-native peer listing capability, then replace the expected-failure assertion with a routed peer contract.

known_gaps.summary: The locked vendor records an in-process teammate's approved graceful shutdown but does not make that teammate inactive, so TeamDelete remains blocked and ACP exposes no addressable teammate stop operation.

evidence.detail: The shutdown approval path relies on finding the teammate task in the approving teammate's AppState and aborting its controller.
The real ACP test records shutdown_approved, then asserts TeamDelete still returns the active-member failure and closes the session to stop the process.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Fix in-process shutdown approval to abort the parent-owned teammate task, or expose an ACP operation that addresses and stops a team peer before TeamDelete retries cleanup.

known_gaps.summary: The locked vendor compiles Agent trigger support, but its management entry point is a local-jsx command and its scheduler is mounted by the REPL lifecycle; neither trigger registration nor trigger-fired prompts are exposed through the current ACP session surface.

evidence.detail: The trigger management command is registered as local-jsx and therefore is absent from ACP available prompt commands.
Local scheduled Agent prompts are delivered by a REPL-mounted hook rather than an ACP lifecycle service.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Expose trigger registry operations and trigger-fired prompt events through ACP; then implement the durable scheduler and remote-provider profile in Phase 7.

known_gaps.summary: RemoteTrigger cannot be enabled in the base profile without an authenticated callback provider, credentials, and an ACP-visible registration lifecycle.

evidence.detail: RemoteTriggerTool is conditionally assembled behind AGENT_TRIGGERS_REMOTE rather than exposed as an ACP operation.
The real Gateway stack rejects remote_trigger creation with HTTP 501 instead of claiming support without credentials or callback ownership.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Define an authenticated remote-trigger Docker profile and expose trigger registration, delivery identity, and acknowledgement through ACP before marking this capability invocable.

known_gaps.summary: ACP defines available_commands_update, but the locked vendor only schedules it while opening, loading, resuming, or forking a session; project command and Skill file changes are not reloaded in an already-running QueryEngine.

evidence.detail: scheduleAvailableCommandsUpdate is called by session lifecycle methods and has no settings or filesystem watcher subscription.
DeepHarness consumes every available_commands_update in real time but keeps the catalog tied to ACP authority instead of making newly scanned files falsely callable.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add an upstream ACP command reload operation or emit available_commands_update after vendor command and Skill discovery invalidation; then add a same-session create/delete contract and remove the restart requirement.

known_gaps.summary: The locked vendor has internal context analysis and CtxInspectTool, but CONTEXT_COLLAPSE is not compiled and ACP exposes only usage_update rather than a structured context inspection operation.

evidence.detail: CtxInspectTool is only assembled when CONTEXT_COLLAPSE is compiled.
The real stack verifies CONTEXT_COLLAPSE is disabled and renders the status instead of exposing a substitute inspection control.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Expose a read-only ACP context inspection method with token categories and no transcript content, then replace the disabled status with the structured projection.

known_gaps.summary: Rewind and its checkpoint alias require the interactive vendor UI; supportsNonInteractive=false prevents ACP session/prompt invocation.

evidence.detail: The rewind command declares supportsNonInteractive=false.
The Session Context API exposes rewind as blocked with its ACP reason and no callable endpoint.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add an ACP rewind operation with explicit target message, diff preview, confirmation, and transcript branch semantics before enabling a Web control.

known_gaps.summary: ACP reduces compact_boundary to fixed assistant text and does not forward trigger, pre-token count, summarized-message count, or boundary identity.

evidence.detail: The compact boundary is converted to the fixed text 'Compacting completed.' without structured metadata.
The real stack suppresses the fixed text and recovers metadata from the vendor transcript as a clearly labeled secondary source.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Add a structured ACP compact notification carrying boundary id, trigger, preTokens, messagesSummarized, and completion status; then remove transcript reconciliation.

known_gaps.summary: Memory extraction and Lodestone run inside vendor housekeeping but have no dedicated ACP lifecycle, result, or configuration status events.

evidence.detail: Lodestone and extraction are scheduled internally by vendor housekeeping.
The Context Inspector renders these capabilities as kernel managed and includes the evidence-backed reason.

known_gaps.upstream_strategy: Expose privacy-preserving ACP housekeeping status events for scheduling, success/failure, and affected memory store identifiers without memory content.
